That same tracking file notes that the very next step is to have a person actually test this fix by logging in on a real device, and that device verification has not happened yet as of this commit, so the work looks complete and consistent with what it claims, but it has not been confirmed working in practice. Given all that, this is best described as code complete rather than tested. Follow-up for the developer: when/how will this be tested, and what's the ETA?

This commit switches the local backend demo's tunnel from Cloudflare to a free ngrok static domain, after the paid Cloudflare named-tunnel option was ruled out. It also re-explains an earlier note that ngrok breaks secure connections, showing instead that the real cause was ngrok's free-tier browser-warning page, fixed by sending a specific header (ngrok-skip-browser-warning) on every request. The actual code and documentation changes in this diff back up that story: the start-demo.sh script now points at the ngrok domain instead of Cloudflare, and the commit's own activity log shows curl checks being run against the tunnel with that header to confirm it returns a working response. That said, the commit's own notes are explicit that the matching change on the app side (adding that same header to the frontend's API calls) has not been made yet and is handed off to a different agent for a later session, with a full recheck on an actual device still expected after that. Because that piece is explicitly still open, this is best described as code complete rather than fully tested. No specific product story was tied to this commit, but that appears fine since the commit explains its own purpose clearly as a self-contained infrastructure change. Nothing in the diff looks like it bundles in unrelated material, and no files were deleted without explanation. Follow-up for the developer: when/how will this be tested, and what's the ETA?
